security_audit.summary: All 65 static findings are false positives involving Rust APIs, Markdown formatting, illustrative requests, and documentation links. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious command execution. Two semantic findings identify data-loss risks from predictable temporary paths and availability risks from unchecked string slicing in examples.

remediation.issue: Test examples use predictable temporary paths and delete or overwrite contents without exclusive ownership checks.
remediation.suggestion: Use tempfile::TempDir and NamedTempFile with exclusive creation and automatic cleanup. Never recursively delete a shared temporary directory.

remediation.issue: String preview and truncation examples slice arbitrary UTF-8 strings at unchecked byte offsets.
remediation.suggestion: Truncate using character iteration or validated character boundaries. Test short strings, empty strings, and multibyte input.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temporary Paths Can Cause Data Loss
semantic_findings.description: The fixture reuses temp_dir().join("test") and recursively deletes it on drop. Another example overwrites and deletes a fixed temporary filename. Existing contents can be lost, and precreated links can redirect writes when these examples run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples use fixed names, nonexclusive creation, and destructive cleanup without proving ownership. This creates data-loss and path-precreation risks if copied and executed.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked String Slicing Can Panic
semantic_findings.description: The preview slices a generated string at byte 50 without checking length or character boundaries. The truncation helper also slices at an unchecked UTF-8 boundary. Adapted applications processing untrusted text can panic, creating an availability risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Rust string indexing panics on short strings or invalid character boundaries. These checks are absent; service impact depends on how the examples are integrated.

content.value_statement: Ownership errors, complex traits, and asynchronous workflows can make Rust development difficult. This skill provides implementation guidance and focused references for safer code and targeted validation.
actual_capabilities: Explain ownership, borrowing, lifetime annotations, smart pointers, and pinned values with Rust examples.
Guide trait design using generics, associated types, trait objects, derive macros, and sealed traits.
Structure recoverable errors with Result, Option, thiserror, anyhow, and contextual propagation.
Guide Tokio tasks, channels, shared state, timeouts, cancellation, and graceful shutdown.
Provide patterns for unit tests, doctests, integration tests, property tests, mocks, benchmarks, and fuzzing.
Direct validation through Cargo formatting, Clippy, tests, doctests, and benchmarks.
limitations: This is instructional Markdown, not a compiler, runtime, or executable testing service.
Compilation and validation require a configured Rust project, toolchain, dependencies, and tool access.
Several examples are incomplete or require adaptation; some use nightly features.
Examples contain temporary-path and string-slicing risks; generated changes require independent review.

use_cases.title: Resolve Borrowing Errors

use_cases.title: Structure an Async Service

use_cases.title: Strengthen Library APIs and Tests
use_cases.description: Review trait boundaries, structured errors, documentation examples, and property tests before a library release.

prompt_templates.title: Understand an Ownership Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the ownership error in [Rust snippet] using [compiler diagnostic]. Suggest the smallest correction and explain why it works.

prompt_templates.title: Introduce Structured Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [Rust function] to propagate recoverable errors with Result and thiserror. Preserve behavior and add tests for failure cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Trait-Based API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Rust API] for ownership, trait bounds, and associated types. Compare static and dynamic dispatch, then propose tests and documentation examples.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tokio Concurrency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Tokio service] for blocking work, task growth, shared locks, cancellation, timeouts, and shutdown. Propose changes and tests; distinguish verified results from recommendations.

output_examples.input: Explain why returning a reference to a local String fails.
output: The local String is dropped when the function returns, so the returned reference would outlive its value.
Return an owned String or borrow data supplied by the caller.
A lifetime annotation cannot extend the lifetime of a local value.

output_examples.input: Review an async worker that holds a shared lock while awaiting a network request.
output: Read the needed state inside a short lock scope, then release the lock before awaiting network I/O.
Apply a timeout and propagate network failures through a structured error type.
Add cancellation and shutdown tests. Run the project checks before claiming the change is validated.

output_examples.input: Suggest a testing strategy for a Rust text parser.
output: Cover empty input, malformed text, multibyte characters, and boundary lengths with unit tests.
Use property tests for invariants and fuzzing for unexpected input.
Keep filesystem fixtures isolated with uniquely created temporary directories.

best_practices: Provide a minimal reproducer, compiler diagnostics, dependency versions, and the intended behavior.
Request explicit ownership decisions, recoverable error handling, and tests for boundary conditions.
Review examples before reuse and validate changes with formatting, Clippy, and relevant project tests.
anti_patterns: Adding clones or broad lifetime annotations without understanding the ownership problem.
Treating example snippets as production-ready or claiming success without running checks.
Running unfamiliar project tests or build scripts with sensitive credentials or elevated privileges.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does this skill compile or test code itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and references; the assistant needs access to your project and Rust tools to execute checks.

faq.question: Can it help with borrowing and lifetime errors?
faq.answer: Yes. The ownership reference covers moves, borrowing, lifetime annotations, smart pointers, interior mutability, and pinning.

faq.question: Does it cover asynchronous Rust?
faq.answer: Yes. The Tokio reference covers tasks, channels, locks, streams, cancellation, timeouts, and graceful shutdown.

faq.question: Are all examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Some snippets need missing types or project setup, and the audit identifies temporary-path and string-slicing risks.

faq.question: Does it require nightly Rust?
faq.answer: Some reference sections explicitly use nightly features. Check each example against your toolchain before adopting it.
